minutes.headline: Parks Commission heard skate park, youth baseball and Marshall Park updates; no formal votes beyond adjournment.
minutes.summary: The commission heard a skate park design and permitting update, a new youth baseball league president's introduction, and the new facilities director's first report. The chair then covered field maintenance requests, summer camps, snowmobile damage, the 51 Parameter Road land question, a parking policy draft, a proposed Marshall Park subcommittee, and the engineering bid draft. Minutes approval was postponed. The only recorded motion was adjournment, and the next meeting was set for March 22.

votes.motion: Approval of prior minutes postponed for vetting (no vote taken)
Motion to adjourn at 9:44 pm, seconded by Chris; roll call taken

budget_items.what_was_said: The skate park group said it is nearly at its fundraising goal and no donors have sought naming rights. The chair asked that any naming rights be discussed with the commission first.

budget_items.topic: Marshall Park funding request to select board
budget_items.what_was_said: The chair said the commission may present to the select board for funds from the town's available balance. Engineering funds were already received last November.
The facilities director said the current landscaping company is under contract until June of next year, so the town is stuck with it for now.
The facilities director has an initial contractor price and will check one more local contractor to try to save money.
Repair depends on funding, and the Powell family and volunteers are looking at ways to help keep the cost low.
Quotes for schematic design were received from Walla and Meridian, with prices typically a percentage of project cost; the deliverables matter more.
A member advised making the fence safe without large spending since the area may be redone under the Marshall Park master plan.

decisions.decision: Approval of the previous minutes was postponed so they could be vetted.
Skate park group agreed to work with the commission on a timeline to draft and finalize the right-of-entry/agreement language.
Commission members to meet again with town counsel on the right-of-entry wording.
Chair will do due diligence on the 51 Parameter Road property over a couple of months and report back.
Chair will research the mechanism for a Marshall Park subcommittee and bring a draft to the next meeting; Pat volunteered to serve.

Draft parking policy to go to the town manager and town counsel; language agreed to include no overnight parking and no vehicles on fields, playgrounds or courts without facilities department approval.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission held no formal votes; the only recorded motion was adjournment, and the next meeting was set for March 22.
The skate park group agreed to work with the commission on a timeline to draft and finalize right-of-entry agreement language.
The commission will meet again with town counsel on the right-of-entry wording for the skate park.
A draft parking policy will go to the town manager and town counsel, with no overnight parking and no vehicles on fields, playgrounds or courts without approval.
The chair will draft a mechanism for a Marshall Park construction subcommittee and research the 51 Parameter Road property, reporting back.

why_it_matters: Marshall Park work and a possible request to the select board for town funds would be a spending decision residents may be asked to weigh in on.
The parking policy would set rules for using town fields, playgrounds and courts, and the skate park agreement would set the terms under which a privately fundraised facility is built on town land.
watch_next: The commission's next meeting on March 22, where the chair is to bring a draft for a Marshall Park subcommittee.
The draft parking policy's review by the town manager and town counsel, and the date for a Marshall Park presentation to the select board, which was left open.
